title: You have made us for yourself (Confessions 1.1)
word: You have made us for yourself
hookLine: the well-known opening: our heart is restless until it rests in you

lines: A MEMOIR THAT STARTS WITH A PRAYER.
WHY CAN'T A HEART SIT STILL?
cards: Memoirs tend to open with a birthplace, a family, a first memory. Augustine sat down to tell his life, and his first words aren't about himself at all.
They're spoken to God, in the old thou and thee, and we're allowed to overhear. Why open a life story with a prayer?
Because the whole story turns on one question, the kind that shows up at three in the morning: why can't a heart sit still?

teach.b: Here's how the Confessions open, in Pusey's old translation: "Great art Thou, O Lord, and greatly to be praised; great is Thy power, and Thy wisdom infinite." Those words echo the Psalms.

Then he turns to the small creature doing the praising, and gives his answer: "Thou awakest us to delight in Thy praise; for Thou madest us for Thyself, and our heart is restless, until it repose in Thee."
Repose is the old word for rest. So restlessness isn't only a malfunction. It's a clue.
The heart keeps reaching, for the next thing, the next person, the next win, and nothing quite settles it, because it was made for God. A neighbor says something close.
The Qur'an, in Pickthall's translation: "Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest!" Christians and Muslims both speak of a heart that comes to rest in God. And one honest difference.
Augustine starts from the ache, a heart restless until it arrives, and his book tells a long search. The Qur'an's verse points to something done now, remembering God, which Muslims call dhikr.

teach.h: RESTLESS UNTIL IT RESTS IN YOU.
teach.b: One restless heart, two traditions, each in its own words.

how: Christians read Augustine's Confessions as a book of prayer as well as a life story, and its line about the restless heart is quoted in sermons and in books on prayer.

games.q: what does “you have made us for yourself” mean?
o: made for God, so the heart rests only in God
made for ourselves, so happiness is up to us
made by our parents, so we owe them our lives

s: the Confessions open with Augustine's birth and family
they open with a prayer: great art Thou, O Lord, and greatly to be praised.
in Augustine's line, restlessness is just a flaw to fix
the popular reading. he says God made us for himself, so the heart keeps reaching.

games.q: a friend keeps switching plans: new major, new city, new everything, and says she's 'just restless'. what would Augustine's opening suggest?
o: the restlessness is a glitch; ignore it and pick one.
the restlessness may point at something no plan can settle.
the restlessness means the perfect plan is still out there.
games.why: Augustine reads the heart's restlessness as a clue: made for God, it keeps reaching until it rests in God.

practice: Let your hands rest and your breath find its own pace. Pick the quietest sound in the room, a fan, a fridge, traffic far off, and rest your attention on it.
When the pull toward the next thing comes, notice it, and come back to the sound.

wordCard.voice: You have made us for yourself. The prayer that opens Augustine's Confessions: made for God, the heart keeps searching until it rests in God.
